questions.stem: A table t(a, b) has the rows (7, 2), (4, 2), (9, 5) and (6, 1). How many rows does `WHERE a > 5 AND b < 3` select?
questions.explain: (7, 2) and (6, 1) pass both tests. (4, 2) fails a > 5 and (9, 5) fails b < 3.

questions.stem: Which condition is equivalent to NOT (a > 5 OR b < 3)?
questions.explain: De Morgan: NOT (p OR q) is (NOT p) AND (NOT q). The opposite of a > 5 is a ≤ 5 and the opposite of b < 3 is b ≥ 3.
The intersection is {2, 3}, the elements that appear in both sets.

questions.stem: R(name, age) = {(A, 20), (B, 25), (C, 20)}. How many tuples does π_age(R) have, when the result is a set?
questions.explain: Projection keeps the age column: 20, 25, 20. As a set, the repeated 20 is dropped, leaving 2 tuples.

questions.stem: R(A, B) = {(1, x), (2, y)} and S(B, C) = {(x, 5), (z, 6)}. How many rows does the natural join R ⋈ S have?
questions.explain: Rows join when their B values match. Only (1, x) and (x, 5) match, giving (1, x, 5). The B values y and z find no partner.
